small_guidance:
- The conv now dominates (fast_p ~0.94 with the post-conv tail already fused). Tuning the existing two kernels has little headroom — the only small win left is to fuse `mean_invstd_kernel` into a single persistent program per (N,C) with a wider `BLOCK_S` autotune (1024/2048/4096, num_warps 8) and drop the separate launch when S=2520 fits in one block.
- Add a `triton.autotune` to `mean_invstd_kernel` keyed on (N,C,S) and remove the hard-coded `BLOCK_S=1024, num_warps=4` launch args so it can pick wider tiles.
- Consider folding `multiplier * multiplier` clamped-square pattern: precompute `m` and `m*m` once per program in registers (already partly done) — minor.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit gather of the 3×3×3 input patch, K = IC*kd*kh*kw = 81. With OC=16 the GEMM is tiny — use BLOCK_N (spatial) = 64-128, BLOCK_M (OC) = 16, BLOCK_K = 32/81. Fuse bias add into the epilogue.
- Fuse the conv epilogue directly with `x * multiplier` and write the post-multiplied tensor; better, also accumulate per-(N,C) sum and sumsq into a small auxiliary buffer via atomic adds (or a second pass) so the mean/invstd kernel becomes trivial.
- Use channels-last (NDHWC) layout for the conv output so the subsequent channel-reduction max kernel reads C contiguously, enabling vectorized loads across C and removing the strided gather currently done with `c*S` offsets.
